examined_fields.PROPERTY_NAME: Outcome and value definition with named beneficiary, constraints and time horizon
examined_fields.MECHANISM: Name the beneficiary and desired outcome; state safety, labour, resilience and externality constraints; choose a time horizon; test whether work changes the outcome.
examined_fields.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Multiple plausible outputs compete, resources are material, or local efficiency could displace customer/system value.
examined_fields.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For trivial, reversible work, record a one-sentence purpose and acceptance condition rather than create a value-stream artefact.
examined_fields.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Legitimate beneficiary representation; outcome observability; explicit non-negotiable constraints; authority to stop low-value work.
examined_fields.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Customer rhetoric masks managerial cost goals; one stakeholder's value harms another; short-horizon metrics; unmeasurable outcomes; retrospective rationalisation.
examined_fields.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Lean literature specifies waste more richly than value; customer language can ignore workers, suppliers, public risk and long-term resilience.
examined_fields.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use an explicit value hypothesis with beneficiary, outcome, constraints, evidence threshold, review date and abandonment rule.
examined_fields.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should value be aggregated when customers, workers, suppliers and public safety conflict?

examined_fields.PROPERTY_NAME: End-to-end system boundary and flow/queue/handoff visibility
examined_fields.MECHANISM: Define the relevant path and work classes; observe arrivals, queues, processing, rework, handoffs, dependencies and outcome latency; assign end-to-end ownership.
examined_fields.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Repeated handoffs, unexplained elapsed time, departmental optimisation or customer delay dominate processing time.
examined_fields.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a short single-owner path, a simple trace or sampled timeline is enough; no wall-sized map.
examined_fields.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stable item identity; traceability across boundaries; truthful timestamps/states; an owner able to resolve cross-boundary causes.
examined_fields.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Map theatre; stale diagrams; excessive instrumentation; forced linear path for exploratory work; omission of externalities; local teams unable to change system constraints.
examined_fields.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Value-stream maps are frequently local snapshots and can mistake visible factory-like sequence for the real distributed causal system.
examined_fields.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Maintain the cheapest decision-useful end-to-end model, including feedback/rework loops, queues, dependencies and outcome—not just touch time.
examined_fields.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should boundaries be chosen in multi-product, platform or ecosystem settings without creating an unmanageable total map?

examined_fields.PROPERTY_NAME: Workplace and work-state legibility
examined_fields.MECHANISM: Expose state and limits at the point of work using labels, layout, telemetry, state models or visual cues proportional to decision need.
examined_fields.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Work is repeatedly lost, searched for, misrouted, duplicated or left in an ambiguous state.
examined_fields.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: When state is already obvious and low-risk, use naming conventions or a small status field; do not create ritual boards or audit scoring.
examined_fields.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Shared state definitions; maintenance ownership; accessibility; protection against surveillance and stale displays.
examined_fields.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: 5S audit theatre; cosmetic tidiness; information overload; stale boards; worker surveillance; local legibility hiding end-to-end state.
examined_fields.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Evidence for exact 5S bundles is small and heterogeneous; legibility can become discipline and scoring rather than aid.
examined_fields.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Make the minimum relevant normal/abnormal state visible to people who can act, with freshness, accessibility and ownership controls.

examined_fields.PROPERTY_NAME: Conditional pull/release control and explicit WIP limits
examined_fields.MECHANISM: Set an explicit bound or release rule for active commitments; admit new work when capacity becomes available; define exceptions and service classes.
examined_fields.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Arrival pressure exceeds completion capacity, active work accumulates, or long WIP correlates with delay/quality loss.
examined_fields.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For low-volume work with naturally bounded commitments, use a simple finish-before-start norm or periodic capacity check.
examined_fields.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Observable WIP boundary; stable item definitions; capacity/replenishment capability; priority and exception policy; no hidden pre-entry queue.
examined_fields.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Starvation; hidden backlog before entry; arbitrary limits; gaming item size/status; blocking critical long-lead work; apparent cycle-time gains through exclusion.
examined_fields.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: A pull signal is not trustworthy demand or capacity; board-level limits can displace queues and invite metric gaming.
examined_fields.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use empirical limits by work class, monitor blocked/aged work and total demand, and adapt limits with capacity, variability and service risk.
examined_fields.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What causal evidence is sufficient to distinguish a useful limit from demand suppression or work reclassification?

examined_fields.PROPERTY_NAME: Batch-size economics and small reversible increments
examined_fields.MECHANISM: Model batch benefits against setup, validation, coordination and transport costs; reduce setup first; choose a reversible economic batch.
examined_fields.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Feedback delay or failure blast radius is material and switching/release cost can be reduced.
examined_fields.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: If changes are already tiny or validation has a fixed high cost, keep the economic batch and improve feedback within it.
examined_fields.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Measurable setup/release costs; modular work; validation capability; rollback/recovery; ability to integrate increments.
examined_fields.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: One-piece-flow dogma; fragmentation overhead; excessive coordination; local micro-batches accumulating into system batches; unsafe partial delivery.
examined_fields.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Smallness is not value; a minimum batch can be uneconomic, and knowledge work may require coherent experimental units.
examined_fields.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Select batch size from total economics and reversibility, not a universal minimum; make delayed feedback and blast radius explicit.

examined_fields.PROPERTY_NAME: Setup, changeover, release and feedback latency reduction
examined_fields.MECHANISM: Separate necessary from avoidable setup; externalise safe preparation; simplify interfaces; automate repeatable checks; measure total transition and recovery.
examined_fields.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Setup, integration, release or environment preparation materially determines batch size, delay or downtime.
examined_fields.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: If setup is rare and immaterial, document the path and avoid an optimisation programme.
examined_fields.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stable interfaces; safe automation; competent maintainers; configuration control; rollback and qualification.
examined_fields.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Unsafe shortcuts; preparation shifted to another team; brittle automation; ergonomic or quality risk; faster release of low-value work.
examined_fields.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Local setup savings often omit preparation, validation and recovery transferred elsewhere.

examined_fields.PROPERTY_NAME: Demand-capacity pacing and production levelling
examined_fields.MECHANISM: Estimate sustainable pace by work class; level the predictable component; explicitly buffer residual variation; replan when assumptions break.
examined_fields.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Repeatable work, measurable aggregate demand, flexible capacity and feasible mix sequencing.
examined_fields.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For unique, exploratory or very low-volume work, use finite-capacity planning, rolling forecasts and explicit priority rather than takt ceremony.
examined_fields.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Demand information; cross-trained/flexible resources; setup capability; exception policy; workload and ergonomic safeguards; buffers.
examined_fields.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: False precision; backlog or overtime used to hide variation; forced pace and work intensification; brittle high-mix schedules; supplier burden transfer.
examined_fields.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Takt can become a coercive pace standard; conventional levelling has weak applicability in high-mix/low-volume or discovery work.
examined_fields.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Level only forecastable aggregate demand, maintain capacity/time buffers and protect workload limits; treat takt as diagnostic, not a metronome.
examined_fields.OPEN_QUESTIONS: Robust rules for levelling highly variable knowledge work remain unresolved; evidence is dominated by manufacturing cases.

examined_fields.PROPERTY_NAME: Explicit buffer portfolio and strategic slack
examined_fields.MECHANISM: Distinguish physical inventory, capacity and time buffers from enabling information, alternate designs/sources and recovery options. Model variability, lead time, consequence and feasible recovery; assign proportionate purpose, sizing, ownership and change triggers.
examined_fields.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Variability or disruption cannot be eliminated economically and service or failure consequences are material.
examined_fields.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For low-risk, rapidly recoverable work, keep only a small contingency and explicit recovery path.
examined_fields.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Demand/failure data; risk appetite; cross-boundary cost visibility; authority to hold reserve; anti-hoarding review.
examined_fields.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Slack becomes unmanaged delay; reserves are raided for utilisation; inventory obsolescence; redundancy hides defects; false quantitative precision.
examined_fields.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Classic Lean rhetoric often treats inventory and slack as waste, while disruption and inventory-performance evidence shows non-monotonic returns.
examined_fields.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Optimise a portfolio of justified buffers; distinguish protective reserve from accidental queue and continuously reassess assumptions.
examined_fields.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should correlated and deep-tier risks be priced when probabilities are poorly known?

examined_fields.PROPERTY_NAME: Flow and queue-aware capacity over maximum local utilisation
examined_fields.MECHANISM: Measure queue age/size and end-to-end throughput; reserve response capacity; subordinate nonconstraints; stop releasing work that worsens congestion.
examined_fields.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Queues grow despite high activity or local productivity gains fail to improve total outcome.
examined_fields.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For low variability and ample capacity, simple utilisation monitoring plus exception handling is enough.
examined_fields.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Valid system boundary; capacity/arrival data; authority across silos; protected slack; outcome measures.
examined_fields.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Underutilisation without purpose; politically contested spare capacity; local teams penalised for system choices; bottleneck migration.
examined_fields.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Lean deployments may still pursue labour or machine utilisation and headcount reduction despite flow doctrine.
examined_fields.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Optimise end-to-end service and total buffering cost; treat utilisation as a constraint or signal, not a target to maximise.
examined_fields.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should public or safety-critical systems value reserve capacity whose benefit appears only during peaks?

examined_fields.PROPERTY_NAME: Demand and replenishment information integrity
examined_fields.MECHANISM: Define signal source, semantics, freshness, authority, forecast complement and exception path; reconcile consumption with long-lead and capacity data.
examined_fields.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Replenishment or release decisions rely on demand signals across time or organisational boundaries.
examined_fields.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For direct low-volume requests, use explicit confirmation and a simple backlog.
examined_fields.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Trusted item identity; data quality; latency bounds; incentives that do not reward signal manipulation; long-lead visibility.
examined_fields.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Demand is endogenous or manipulated; urgent work bypasses signals; forecasts ignored; local pull cannot prepare long-lead components.
examined_fields.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: A visible pull signal does not establish trustworthy demand or adequate replenishment capability.
examined_fields.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A governed demand-information contract, not blind reaction to the latest request.

examined_fields.PROPERTY_NAME: Abnormality detection and signalling
examined_fields.MECHANISM: Define detectable abnormal states and confidence; instrument or enable human recognition; signal with severity, location, owner and time.
examined_fields.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Continued operation after an abnormality materially increases harm, rework, delay or uncertainty.
examined_fields.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For rare, low-consequence events, use a manual report with clear ownership rather than continuous instrumentation.
examined_fields.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Known normal envelope; usable detectors; low-friction human signalling; response ownership; alarm review.
examined_fields.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: False alarms, missed detections, alarm fatigue, ambiguous ownership, suppressed signals and throughput pressure.

examined_fields.PROPERTY_NAME: Bounded stop, containment, escalation and recovery authority
examined_fields.MECHANISM: Define severity-based authority to hold, stop, isolate or degrade service; summon support; specify restart/recovery criteria and appeal.
examined_fields.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Expected propagation harm exceeds interruption and recovery cost, or safety/quality boundaries are breached.
examined_fields.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For low-consequence reversible anomalies, flag and route to a bounded follow-up queue without stopping the whole system.

examined_fields.PROPERTY_NAME: Quality at source and defect containment
examined_fields.MECHANISM: Place proportionate checks near creation; isolate failed output; preserve trace/evidence; repair or reject under defined criteria.
examined_fields.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Defects become more costly or less diagnosable downstream, and source checks have useful sensitivity.
examined_fields.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For very low-risk reversible output, use sampled or downstream validation with traceability.
examined_fields.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Testability; clear quality criteria; containment path; no incentive to hide defects; qualified repair/release.
